topics.name: Worry and anxiety
topics.question: What do I do when I can't stop worrying?
topics.summary: Worry pulls tomorrow's troubles into today. Scripture's answer is not to stop caring, but to hand the care to God.
topics.guidance: Jesus does not tell worried people to try harder. He points them to a Father who feeds the birds and knows what they need, and tells them to put his kingdom first and take one day at a time. The apostles turn that into a habit: bring every care to God in prayer, with thanks, and his peace will guard your heart and mind.

teachings.note: Put God's kingdom first; let tomorrow look after itself.
teachings.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.  Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

teachings.note: Turn every worry into prayer, with thanks, and God's peace will guard you.
teachings.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

teachings.note: Throw your cares on God, because he cares for you.
teachings.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

teachings.note: A mind that rests on God is kept in peace.
teachings.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.

teachings.note: Hand your burden to the LORD; he will hold you up.
teachings.text: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

topics.practice: When a worry comes, turn it into a one-line prayer, then name one thing you are thankful for.
topics.prayer: Father, you know what I need before I ask. I give you what I am carrying today, and I trust you with tomorrow.

topics.name: Fear and courage
topics.question: How can I be brave when I'm afraid?
topics.summary: Courage in the Bible is not the absence of fear. It is trusting that God is with you in it.
topics.guidance: 'Fear not' is one of the most repeated commands in Scripture, and it almost always comes with a reason: 'for I am with thee'. God does not ask his people to feel strong. He asks them to remember who goes with them, and to take the next step.

teachings.note: Jesus gives a peace the world cannot give, so don't let your heart be afraid.
teachings.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

teachings.note: Be strong and brave, because God goes with you wherever you go.
teachings.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

teachings.note: Don't be afraid: God is with you and will hold you up.
teachings.text: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

teachings.note: If the LORD is your light and strength, whom do you need to fear?
teachings.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

teachings.note: God's Spirit is not one of fear, but of power, love and a sound mind.
teachings.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

teachings.note: Being loved completely drives fear out.
teachings.text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.

topics.practice: Name the fear out loud, then say who is with you in it. Take one small step anyway.
topics.prayer: Lord, I am afraid. Remind me that you are with me, and give me courage for the next step.

topics.name: Anger
topics.question: What do I do with my anger?
topics.summary: Anger is not always sin, but it must not be kept, fed or acted on in revenge.
topics.guidance: The Bible expects us to feel anger and warns us not to let it rule. Deal with it quickly, before the day ends; listen more than you speak; answer softly. Jesus takes it further: if someone has something against you, go and make peace before you go to worship.

teachings.note: Put things right with your brother before you bring your gift to God.
teachings.text: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;  Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

teachings.note: Be angry without sinning, and don't go to bed angry.
teachings.text: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath: Neither give place to the devil.

teachings.note: Be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to anger.
teachings.text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

teachings.note: A gentle answer calms anger; harsh words stir it up.
teachings.text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

teachings.note: Ruling your own temper takes more strength than capturing a city.
teachings.text: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

teachings.note: God asks the angry prophet a question worth asking ourselves: is this anger right?
teachings.text: Then said the LORD, Doest thou well to be angry?

topics.practice: Before you answer in anger, wait, and ask God's question: 'Doest thou well to be angry?'
topics.prayer: Lord, slow me down. Help me to listen before I speak, and to make peace before the sun goes down.

topics.name: Pride and humility
topics.question: How do I stay humble?
topics.summary: Pride puts self at the centre. Humility is not thinking less of yourself, but thinking of others and of God first.
topics.guidance: Scripture turns the world's ladder upside down: the one who lifts himself up is brought down, and the one who humbles himself is lifted up. Humility is walking with God and counting other people's needs as important as your own.

teachings.note: Whoever raises himself up will be brought down, and the humble will be raised.
teachings.text: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

teachings.note: The greatest in God's kingdom is the one who becomes humble like a little child.
teachings.text: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

teachings.note: What God asks: do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with him.
teachings.text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

teachings.note: Pride comes before a fall.
teachings.text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

teachings.note: Think of others as better than yourself, and look to their interests too.
teachings.text: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

teachings.note: Humble yourself before God, and he will lift you up.
teachings.text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

topics.practice: Today, quietly do something for someone that no one will thank you for.
topics.prayer: Lord, keep me low before you. Teach me to walk humbly and to put others first.

topics.name: Contentment
topics.question: Why am I never satisfied?
topics.summary: Contentment is learned, not bought. It grows from knowing that God will never leave you.
topics.guidance: The Bible is blunt that more money and more things do not satisfy. Paul says he had to learn contentment, in plenty and in need, and that the secret was Christ's strength. Hebrews gives the reason we can be content: God has promised never to leave us.

teachings.note: Life is not measured by how much you own.
teachings.text: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

teachings.note: Paul learned to be content with much or little, through Christ's strength.
teachings.text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

teachings.note: Godliness with contentment is great gain; we brought nothing in and take nothing out.
teachings.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.

teachings.note: Be content, because God has said he will never leave you.
teachings.text: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

teachings.note: Whoever loves money never has enough of it.
teachings.text: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.

teachings.note: Do not covet what belongs to someone else.
teachings.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.

topics.practice: Write down three things you already have that you once prayed for.
topics.prayer: Lord, you are enough for me. Teach me to be content, and to trust you in plenty and in need.

topics.name: Temptation
topics.question: How do I say no to temptation?
topics.summary: Temptation comes to everyone. God always provides a way out, and his word is the first weapon.
topics.guidance: Jesus was tempted and answered each time with Scripture. He told his friends to watch and pray, because the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak. The apostles add that no temptation is unique and that God always makes a way of escape; Joseph shows what taking it looks like.

teachings.note: Watch and pray: the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.
teachings.text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

teachings.note: Jesus answered temptation with the word of God.
teachings.text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

teachings.note: No temptation is beyond what others face, and God always makes a way out.
teachings.text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.

teachings.note: Temptation grows from our own desires; don't blame God for it.
teachings.text: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.

teachings.note: Guard your heart, because your whole life flows from it.
teachings.text: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.

teachings.note: Joseph refused: how could he do this and sin against God?
teachings.text: There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

topics.practice: Know your weak moment, and plan your way out before it comes.
topics.prayer: Lead me not into temptation, Lord, and show me the way out when it comes.

topics.name: Purity
topics.question: Does God care what I think about and do with my body?
topics.summary: Yes. Purity starts in the heart and the thought life, and the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit.
topics.guidance: Jesus blessed the pure in heart, because they will see God. The Bible treats the body as precious, bought at a price, and asks us to honour God with it. The way to a clean life is to fill the mind with what is true, lovely and good, and to keep to God's word.

teachings.note: The pure in heart are blessed; they shall see God.
teachings.text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

teachings.note: A young person keeps their way clean by living by God's word.
teachings.text: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

teachings.note: Your body is the Holy Spirit's temple, bought at a price; honour God with it.
teachings.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.

teachings.note: Fill your mind with whatever is true, honest, pure and lovely.
teachings.text: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

teachings.note: God's will is that we keep ourselves pure and honour our bodies.
teachings.text: For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication: That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour;

topics.practice: Notice what you feed your eyes and mind on this week, and swap one thing for something good.
topics.prayer: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Help me to honour you with my mind and body.

topics.name: Love
topics.question: What does real love look like?
topics.summary: Love God with everything, and love your neighbour as yourself. Everything else hangs on these two.
topics.guidance: When asked for the greatest commandment, Jesus joined two from the Law: love God, love your neighbour. At the Last Supper he gave a new standard: love one another as I have loved you. Paul spells out what that love looks like day to day, and John says it comes from God, because God is love.

teachings.note: The two great commandments: love God, and love your neighbour as yourself.
teachings.text: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.  This is the first and great commandment.  And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

teachings.note: Love each other as Jesus loved you; that is how the world will know his followers.
teachings.text: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.  By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.

teachings.note: Love is patient and kind; it is not proud, keeps no record of wrongs and never gives up.
teachings.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

teachings.note: Love comes from God, because God is love.
teachings.text: Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

teachings.note: Don't take revenge or hold a grudge; love your neighbour as yourself.
teachings.text: Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.

topics.practice: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4-7 and put your own name in place of 'charity'. Where does it not fit yet?
topics.prayer: Lord, you loved me first. Teach me to love you with all I am, and to love the people around me as you do.

topics.name: Forgiveness
topics.question: How can I forgive someone who hurt me?
topics.summary: We forgive because we have been forgiven. It is not pretending the hurt never happened, but letting God be the judge.
topics.guidance: Jesus links our forgiving to our being forgiven, and told Peter to forgive without counting. On the cross he prayed for the men who crucified him. Forgiveness does not say the wrong was small; Joseph named what his brothers did as evil, and still left the judging to God and cared for them.

teachings.note: Forgive others, as you hope to be forgiven by God.
teachings.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:  But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

teachings.note: Asked if seven times was enough, Jesus said seventy times seven: stop counting.
teachings.text: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

teachings.note: Jesus prayed for those who were killing him.
teachings.text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

teachings.note: Be kind and forgive one another, as God in Christ forgave you.
teachings.text: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.

teachings.note: God delights in mercy and throws our sins into the depths of the sea.
teachings.text: Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy. He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.

teachings.note: Joseph told his brothers: you meant evil, God meant it for good; don't be afraid.
teachings.text: And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.

topics.practice: Name the person. Tell God honestly what they did, then ask him for the strength to release them.
topics.prayer: Father, forgive me as I forgive those who have wronged me. Give me grace to let go of what I cannot carry.

topics.name: Marriage
topics.question: What does God say about marriage?
topics.summary: Marriage is God's idea: two people joined as one for life, loving and serving each other as Christ loves his church.
topics.guidance: From the first pages of the Bible, marriage is a man and woman leaving their parents and becoming one. Jesus affirmed it and said no one should separate what God has joined. The apostles call husbands and wives to put each other first, in the pattern of Christ's own self-giving love.

teachings.note: A man leaves his parents and holds fast to his wife; the two become one.
teachings.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

teachings.note: What God has joined together, let no one separate.
teachings.text: And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female,  And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?  Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

teachings.note: Put each other first, out of reverence for God.
teachings.text: Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.

teachings.note: Husbands, love your wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
teachings.text: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;

teachings.note: Honour marriage and keep it pure.
teachings.text: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

teachings.note: Finding a wife is finding a good thing, and favour from the LORD.
teachings.text: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD.

teachings.note: God witnesses the covenant with the wife of your youth, your companion.
teachings.text: Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.

topics.practice: Ask your husband or wife one question this week: “What can I do to make your day easier?”
topics.prayer: Lord, bless our marriage (or the marriage you have for me). Teach us to love each other as Christ loves us.

topics.name: Parents and children
topics.question: How should families treat each other?
topics.summary: Children are to honour their parents; parents are to teach, train and not provoke their children.
topics.guidance: Honouring father and mother is the first commandment with a promise attached. Parents are given the task of passing on God's words in everyday life: at home, on the road, at bedtime and in the morning. Jesus welcomed children and said the kingdom belongs to them.

teachings.note: Honour your father and mother.
teachings.text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

teachings.note: Keep God's words in your heart and talk about them with your children all day long.
teachings.text: And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

teachings.note: Train a child in the way they should go.
teachings.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

teachings.note: Children are a gift and heritage from the LORD.
teachings.text: Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.

teachings.note: Let the children come to me; the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
teachings.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

teachings.note: Children, obey and honour your parents; fathers, don't provoke your children, but bring them up in the Lord.
teachings.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth. And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

topics.practice: Share one thing God has done for you with your child or parent this week.
topics.prayer: Lord, bless my family. Help us to honour and teach one another in your ways.

topics.name: Friendship
topics.question: What makes a true friend?
topics.summary: A true friend loves at all times, tells the truth, and sticks closer than a brother. Choose friends who make you better.
topics.guidance: Proverbs is full of friendship: loyal in hard times, honest enough to sharpen you, and better than going it alone. Jonathan and David show a friendship that put the other first. Jesus calls his disciples friends, and shows the greatest love a friend can give.

teachings.note: No love is greater than laying down your life for your friends; Jesus calls us his friends.
teachings.text: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.  Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.  Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.

teachings.note: A friend loves at all times.
teachings.text: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

teachings.note: Friends sharpen each other, as iron sharpens iron.
teachings.text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

teachings.note: Two are better than one: if one falls, the other lifts him up.
teachings.text: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.

teachings.note: Jonathan loved David as his own soul.
teachings.text: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

teachings.note: Bad company corrupts good character.
teachings.text: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.

topics.practice: Reach out to a friend who is going through something hard, and just be there.
topics.prayer: Thank you, Jesus, for calling me your friend. Help me to be a faithful friend to others.

topics.name: Loving your enemies
topics.question: How do I treat people who are against me?
topics.summary: Don't repay evil with evil. Bless, pray for and do good to those who hate you, and overcome evil with good.
topics.guidance: Jesus' command to love enemies was not new to the Law, which told Israel to return an enemy's straying ox. But he made it the mark of God's children. The apostles show how: don't take revenge, feed your enemy when he is hungry, and answer insults with blessing.

teachings.note: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
teachings.text: Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.  But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

teachings.note: Do good to those who hate you; bless those who curse you.
teachings.text: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,  Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

teachings.note: Feed a hungry enemy; overcome evil with good.
teachings.text: Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

teachings.note: Don't pay back evil for evil or insult for insult; bless instead.
teachings.text: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.

teachings.note: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread.
teachings.text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

teachings.note: Even your enemy's lost ox should be brought home.
teachings.text: If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again. If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.

topics.practice: Pray by name for someone who has hurt you, and ask God to bless them.
topics.prayer: Lord Jesus, you prayed for your enemies. Soften my heart toward the people who are against me.

topics.name: Words and the tongue
topics.question: Do my words really matter?
topics.summary: Words carry life and death. We will give account for them, so let them build up rather than tear down.
topics.guidance: Jesus said we will answer for every careless word, and that a simple yes or no should be enough. James calls the tongue a small fire that can burn a forest. Proverbs puts it plainly: words can wound like a sword or heal like medicine.

teachings.note: We will give account for every careless word we speak.
teachings.text: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.  For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

teachings.note: Let your yes mean yes and your no mean no.
teachings.text: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

teachings.note: The same mouth shouldn't bless God and curse people.
teachings.text: Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God. Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

teachings.note: Speak only what builds others up and gives grace to those who hear.
teachings.text: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.

teachings.note: Death and life are in the power of the tongue.
teachings.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

teachings.note: A prayer: set a guard over my mouth.
teachings.text: Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.

topics.practice: For one day, say nothing about anyone that you wouldn't say to their face.
topics.prayer: Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth. Let my words today build up and not tear down.

topics.name: Work
topics.question: Does my work matter to God?
topics.summary: Work was part of God's good plan before the fall. Whatever you do, do it with all your heart, as for the Lord.
topics.guidance: Before sin entered the world, God put Adam in the garden to work it and keep it. Work is not a curse but a calling. The Bible praises diligence and warns against idleness, and Paul tells even slaves to work 'heartily, as to the Lord', because he is the one who rewards.

teachings.note: God gave the first man work: to tend and keep the garden.
teachings.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

teachings.note: Jesus said his Father is always at work, and so is he.
teachings.text: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.

teachings.note: Whatever you do, do it with all your might.
teachings.text: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

teachings.note: Hard work brings profit; mere talk leads to poverty.
teachings.text: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.

teachings.note: Work wholeheartedly, as for the Lord and not for people.
teachings.text: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ.

teachings.note: Whoever refuses to work should not expect to eat.
teachings.text: For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.

topics.practice: Before you start work tomorrow, offer it to God in one sentence.
topics.prayer: Lord, my work belongs to you. Help me to do it well and honestly, as for you.

topics.name: Money and possessions
topics.question: How should I think about money?
topics.summary: Money is a good servant and a terrible master. You cannot serve God and money.
topics.guidance: Jesus spoke about money more than almost anything else, because it so easily takes God's place. Store up treasure in heaven, he said, because your heart follows your treasure. Paul warns that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, and tells the rich to be generous and hope in God, not in wealth.

teachings.note: Store up treasure in heaven; your heart follows your treasure.
teachings.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:  But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:  For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

teachings.note: No one can serve two masters: God and money.
teachings.text: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

teachings.note: The love of money is a root of every kind of evil.
teachings.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

teachings.note: Tell the rich to trust God, not riches, and to be generous.
teachings.text: Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy; That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.

teachings.note: A wise prayer: give me neither poverty nor riches, just my daily bread.
teachings.text: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.

teachings.note: When God is left out, wages go into a bag with holes.
teachings.text: Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.

topics.practice: Look at where your money went last month. What does it say your heart treasures?
topics.prayer: Lord, everything I have is yours. Keep me from loving money, and make me generous.

topics.name: Generosity
topics.question: How much should I give?
topics.summary: Give freely, cheerfully and in proportion to what you have. God loves a cheerful giver, and no one out-gives him.
topics.guidance: Jesus praised a widow who gave two small coins, because she gave all she had. The Law told Israel to open their hands wide to the poor and to bring the tithe. Paul says each should give as they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly, for God loves a cheerful giver.

teachings.note: Give, and it will be given to you, pressed down and running over.
teachings.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

teachings.note: The poor widow gave more than all the rich, because she gave everything.
teachings.text: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:  For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

teachings.note: It is more blessed to give than to receive.
teachings.text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

teachings.note: Give as you've decided in your heart; God loves a cheerful giver.
teachings.text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

teachings.note: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD.
teachings.text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

teachings.note: Bring the tithe, and see if God will not pour out a blessing.
teachings.text: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.

teachings.note: Don't harden your heart to a poor brother; open your hand wide.
teachings.text: If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which the LORD thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother: But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

topics.practice: Give something away this week, quietly, to someone who cannot pay you back.
topics.prayer: Generous God, you gave your Son for me. Make me a cheerful giver.

topics.name: Honesty
topics.question: Is a small lie really a big deal?
topics.summary: Yes. God hates a false balance. Faithfulness in small things shows who we are in big ones.
topics.guidance: The Law demanded honest weights and measures in the market. Proverbs says the one who walks in integrity walks securely. Jesus said that faithfulness in very little shows faithfulness in much, and the apostles tell believers to put away lying and speak the truth to one another.

teachings.note: Whoever is faithful in little is faithful in much.
teachings.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

teachings.note: Use honest weights and measures.
teachings.text: Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard, in weight, or in measure. Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have: I am the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt.

teachings.note: God hates a rigged scale and delights in an honest one.
teachings.text: A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.

teachings.note: Whoever walks in integrity walks securely.
teachings.text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

teachings.note: Speak the truth to one another.
teachings.text: These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates:

teachings.note: Put away lying; speak truth, because we belong to each other.
teachings.text: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.

topics.practice: If you have shaded the truth somewhere, go and set it straight.
topics.prayer: Lord of truth, make me honest in small things and large, when I am seen and when I am not.

topics.name: Justice and the poor
topics.question: What does God expect me to do about injustice?
topics.summary: Do justly, love mercy, and speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves. Serving the least is serving Christ.
topics.guidance: The prophets thundered against worship that ignored the poor, the widow and the orphan. The Law built care for the poor into farming itself. Jesus said that whatever we do for the least of his brothers, we do for him, and James calls caring for widows and orphans pure religion.

teachings.note: God requires us to do justly, love mercy and walk humbly.
teachings.text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

teachings.note: Let justice roll down like waters.
teachings.text: But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

teachings.note: Learn to do good: seek justice, help the oppressed, defend the orphan and widow.
teachings.text: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

teachings.note: Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for me.
teachings.text: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

teachings.note: Pure religion: care for orphans and widows, and keep yourself unstained.
teachings.text: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

teachings.note: Speak up for those who cannot speak, and defend the poor.
teachings.text: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

teachings.note: Leave the edges of your field for the poor and the stranger.
teachings.text: And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest. And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am the LORD your God.

topics.practice: Find one person or cause near you that speaks for the voiceless, and give your time or help.
topics.prayer: Lord, open my eyes to the people I pass by. Teach me to do justly and love mercy.

topics.name: Purpose
topics.question: What is my life for?
topics.summary: To know God, love him and enjoy him, and to do everything, even eating and drinking, to his glory.
topics.guidance: The Preacher tried everything under the sun and concluded: fear God and keep his commandments. Jeremiah says the only thing worth boasting about is knowing God. Jesus came so that we might have life to the full, and Paul says that whatever we do, we can do it to the glory of God.

teachings.note: Jesus came so that we may have life, and have it to the full.
teachings.text: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.

teachings.note: Let your light shine so that people see your good works and glorify God.
teachings.text: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

teachings.note: Don't boast in wisdom, strength or riches, but in knowing God.
teachings.text: Thus saith the LORD, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD.

teachings.note: The conclusion of it all: fear God and keep his commandments.
teachings.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

teachings.note: Whatever you do, even eating and drinking, do it all for God's glory.
teachings.text: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

topics.practice: At the end of today, ask: where did I see God, and where did I show him to someone?
topics.prayer: Lord, my life is yours. Let me know you, and let my light shine for your glory.

topics.name: Prayer
topics.question: How should I pray?
topics.summary: Simply, honestly and often. Ask, seek and knock; God is near to all who call on him.
topics.guidance: Jesus taught his disciples to pray in secret, not for show, and to keep asking without giving up. He promised that those who ask receive. The apostles say to pray without ceasing and in everything give thanks. The prophets and psalms promise that God is near and answers when we call.

teachings.note: Pray to your Father in secret, and he will reward you.
teachings.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

teachings.note: Ask, seek and knock: everyone who asks receives.
teachings.text: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.  For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

teachings.note: Stay close to Jesus and his words, and ask.
teachings.text: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.

teachings.note: Pray without ceasing, and give thanks in everything.
teachings.text: Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

teachings.note: The earnest prayer of a righteous person is powerful.
teachings.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

teachings.note: Call to God, and he will answer and show you great things.
teachings.text: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

teachings.note: The LORD is near to all who call on him in truth.
teachings.text: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.

topics.practice: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly (Matthew 6:9-13), stopping on each line to make it your own.
topics.prayer: Lord, teach me to pray.

topics.name: Faith and trust
topics.question: How can I trust God when I can't see the way?
topics.summary: Faith is trusting God's word before you see the outcome. Lean on him, not on your own understanding.
topics.guidance: Faith in the Bible is not a feeling but trust in a person. Proverbs says to trust the LORD with all your heart and he will make your paths straight. Habakkuk learned that 'the just shall live by his faith' in the worst of times, and Hebrews defines faith as confidence in what we hope for but cannot yet see.

teachings.note: Have faith in God; believe as you pray.
teachings.text: And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.  For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith.  Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.

teachings.note: Don't let your heart be troubled: trust God, and trust me.
teachings.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.

teachings.note: Trust the LORD with all your heart; he will direct your paths.
teachings.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

teachings.note: The just shall live by faith.
teachings.text: Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.

teachings.note: Faith is being sure of what we hope for and cannot yet see.
teachings.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

teachings.note: Faith grows by hearing the word of God.
teachings.text: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

topics.practice: Write down one promise of God and one situation where you need to trust it today.
topics.prayer: Lord, I trust you with what I cannot see. Direct my path.

topics.name: Knowing God's will
topics.question: How do I know what God wants me to do?
topics.summary: Start with his word, ask for wisdom, listen to wise counsel, and obey what you already know.
topics.guidance: God promises to guide those who seek him. His word is a lamp for the next step, not always a floodlight for the whole road. James promises wisdom to anyone who asks. Paul says a renewed mind learns to recognise God's good will, and Jesus says that willingness to do God's will comes before knowing it.

teachings.note: Whoever is willing to do God's will shall know the truth.
teachings.text: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.

teachings.note: God's word is a lamp for your feet and a light for your path.
teachings.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

teachings.note: God promises to instruct and guide you with his eye upon you.
teachings.text: I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye.

teachings.note: Plans succeed with many advisers.
teachings.text: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

teachings.note: You will hear a word behind you: this is the way, walk in it.
teachings.text: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.

teachings.note: Be transformed by a renewed mind, and you'll recognise God's good will.
teachings.text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

teachings.note: If you lack wisdom, ask God; he gives generously.
teachings.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

topics.practice: Before a decision, pray, read, and ask one wise person you trust.
topics.prayer: Lord, show me the way I should walk. I want to do your will; give me wisdom and light.

topics.name: Rest
topics.question: Is it all right to stop?
topics.summary: Yes. God rested, commanded rest, and invites the weary to come to him. Rest is a gift, not a weakness.
topics.guidance: God rested on the seventh day and made the sabbath a gift for people who would otherwise never stop. Jesus took his tired disciples away to rest, and invited everyone who labours and is heavy laden to come to him. Stillness is where we learn again that he is God and we are not.

teachings.note: God rested on the seventh day and blessed it.
teachings.text: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

teachings.note: Remember the sabbath: six days to work, and one to rest.
teachings.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

teachings.note: Come to me, all who are weary, and I will give you rest.
teachings.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.  Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.  For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

teachings.note: Come away to a quiet place and rest a while.
teachings.text: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

teachings.note: The sabbath was made for people, not people for the sabbath.
teachings.text: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

teachings.note: Be still, and know that I am God.
teachings.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

teachings.note: In returning and rest you are saved; quietness and trust are your strength.
teachings.text: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.

topics.practice: Set aside one unhurried hour this week with no screen, and spend some of it with God.
topics.prayer: Lord, I am tired. I come to you for rest. Teach me to be still and know that you are God.

topics.name: Serving others
topics.question: What does it mean to be great?
topics.summary: In God's kingdom the greatest is the servant. Jesus came not to be served, but to serve.
topics.guidance: Jesus overturned every idea of greatness: the first will be the servant of all. He washed his disciples' feet and told them to do the same. Even Rehoboam's old advisers knew that a leader who serves his people is followed for ever. The apostles call every believer to use their gifts to serve one another in love.

teachings.note: Whoever wants to be great must be the servant of all, as Jesus came to serve.
teachings.text: But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister:  And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.  For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

teachings.note: Jesus washed his disciples' feet and told them to do the same.
teachings.text: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.  For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.

teachings.note: Use your freedom to serve one another in love.
teachings.text: For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.

teachings.note: Have the mind of Christ, who took the form of a servant.
teachings.text: Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:

teachings.note: Use whatever gift you have received to serve others.
teachings.text: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

teachings.note: Serve the people, and they will serve you for ever.
teachings.text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.

topics.practice: Look for the job nobody wants to do this week, and do it.
topics.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to serve. Give me a servant's heart.

topics.name: Suffering
topics.question: Why is this happening to me?
topics.summary: The Bible does not always answer why. It promises that God is with us in suffering, and that he works even this for good.
topics.guidance: Jesus told his friends plainly that in this world they would have trouble, and to take heart because he has overcome the world. Job worshipped in his loss without knowing why. The apostles teach that suffering can grow patience and hope, that our troubles are light beside the glory coming, and that God works all things together for good for those who love him.

teachings.note: You will have trouble in this world, but take heart: I have overcome the world.
teachings.text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

teachings.note: The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be his name.
teachings.text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

teachings.note: When you pass through deep waters and fire, God will be with you.
teachings.text: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.

teachings.note: God works all things together for good for those who love him.
teachings.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

teachings.note: Suffering produces patience, character and a hope that does not disappoint.
teachings.text: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.

teachings.note: Our troubles are light and brief next to the glory to come.
teachings.text: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

teachings.note: Trials test faith and make us complete.
teachings.text: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

topics.practice: Tell God honestly how you feel. The Psalms give you permission to lament.
topics.prayer: Lord, I don't understand this. Be with me in it, and work even this for good.

topics.name: Grief and loss
topics.question: How do I grieve as a believer?
topics.summary: Grieve honestly, as Jesus did. But not as those who have no hope.
topics.guidance: Jesus wept at his friend's grave, though he knew he would raise him. Grief is not a lack of faith. The Bible gives a time to weep, promises that God is close to the broken-hearted, and that joy will come in the morning. Paul does not tell grieving believers not to sorrow, but not to sorrow without hope.

teachings.note: Those who mourn are blessed: they will be comforted.
teachings.text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

teachings.note: Jesus grieved openly at his friend's grave, though he was about to raise him.
teachings.text: Jesus wept.

teachings.note: The LORD is close to the broken-hearted.
teachings.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

teachings.note: Weeping may last for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
teachings.text: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.

teachings.note: There is a time to weep and a time to mourn.
teachings.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted; A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up; A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

teachings.note: God gives beauty for ashes and joy for mourning.
teachings.text: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.

teachings.note: Grieve, but not like those who have no hope.
teachings.text: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.

topics.practice: Let yourself grieve. Share one memory with someone, and one hope with God.
topics.prayer: Lord, you wept too. Stay close to my broken heart, and hold my hope when I cannot.

topics.name: Discouragement and doubt
topics.question: What do I do when I feel like giving up?
topics.summary: Even prophets despaired. God meets the weary with rest, fresh strength and mercies that are new every morning.
topics.guidance: Elijah asked to die under a juniper tree, and God sent food and sleep before he sent new work. The Psalms talk honestly to a downcast soul. Thomas doubted, and Jesus came to him. The promise is not that we will never tire, but that God gives power to the faint and his mercies never run out.

teachings.note: Jesus came to doubting Thomas and invited him to believe.
teachings.text: Then saith he to Thomas, reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

teachings.note: Get up and eat, because the journey is too much for you.
teachings.text: And the angel of the LORD came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee.

teachings.note: God gives power to the faint; those who wait on him renew their strength.
teachings.text: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

teachings.note: God's mercies never end; they are new every morning.
teachings.text: It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

teachings.note: Why so downcast, my soul? Hope in God.
teachings.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.    Psalm 43

teachings.note: Don't grow weary of doing good; the harvest will come.
teachings.text: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

topics.practice: Eat, sleep and rest, then tell God honestly where you are.
topics.prayer: Lord, I'm tired and my faith is small. Renew my strength, and help my unbelief.

topics.name: Loneliness
topics.question: What if I feel completely alone?
topics.summary: God has promised never to leave you or forsake you. He sets the lonely in families.
topics.guidance: Moses told Israel, and later Joshua, that God would never fail or forsake them. David wrote that even if father and mother abandon us, the LORD takes us in. Paul, deserted by everyone at his trial, wrote that the Lord stood with him. And Jesus' last words in Matthew are a promise: I am with you always.

teachings.note: I am with you always, to the end of the age.
teachings.text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

teachings.note: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
teachings.text: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.

teachings.note: God will never fail you or forsake you.
teachings.text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

teachings.note: Even if my parents forsake me, the LORD will take me in.
teachings.text: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.

teachings.note: God sets the lonely in families.
teachings.text: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.

teachings.note: Everyone deserted me, but the Lord stood with me and strengthened me.
teachings.text: At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.

topics.practice: Reach out to one person today, even with a short message. Someone else may be lonely too.
topics.prayer: Lord, you are with me even here. Set me in a family of your people.

topics.name: Hope
topics.question: Is there hope for my future?
topics.summary: Yes. God has plans for his people, and a living hope kept in heaven that nothing can spoil.
topics.guidance: Jeremiah wrote to exiles far from home that God's thoughts toward them were of peace, to give them a future. The apostles call Christian hope 'lively', alive because Jesus rose, and an anchor for the soul. Hope in the Bible is not wishful thinking but confident waiting on a faithful God.

teachings.note: God's thoughts toward his people are of peace, to give them a future.
teachings.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

teachings.note: The LORD is my portion, so I will hope in him.
teachings.text: The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.

teachings.note: What am I waiting for? My hope is in you.
teachings.text: And now, Lord, what wait I for? my hope is in thee.

teachings.note: A living hope through Jesus' resurrection, and an inheritance that cannot fade.
teachings.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,

teachings.note: Hope is an anchor for the soul, sure and steady.
teachings.text: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;

teachings.note: May the God of hope fill you with joy and peace.
teachings.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.

topics.practice: Write down one fear about the future, and next to it one promise of God.
topics.prayer: God of hope, fill me with joy and peace as I trust you with my future.

topics.name: Death and eternal life
topics.question: What happens when we die?
topics.summary: For those who trust Christ, death is not the end. Whoever believes in him has everlasting life and will be raised.
topics.guidance: Job believed that his Redeemer lives and that he would see God. Daniel foresaw the dead awaking. Jesus promised everlasting life to all who believe, called himself the resurrection and the life, and said he was preparing a place for his people. Paul could say that to die is gain, because death has lost its sting.

teachings.note: Whoever believes in God's Son will not perish but have everlasting life.
teachings.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

teachings.note: I am the resurrection and the life; whoever believes in me will live.
teachings.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:  And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?

teachings.note: In my Father's house are many rooms; I go to prepare a place for you.
teachings.text: In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

teachings.note: I know that my Redeemer lives, and I will see God.
teachings.text: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:

teachings.note: Even in the valley of the shadow of death, you are with me.
teachings.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

teachings.note: Those who sleep in the dust will awake.
teachings.text: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

teachings.note: Death is swallowed up in victory: where is its sting?
teachings.text: So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?

teachings.note: To live is Christ, and to die is gain.
teachings.text: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

topics.practice: Read John 11:25-26 and answer Jesus' question to Martha for yourself: 'Believest thou this?'
topics.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life. I put my trust in you, in life and in death.

topics.name: The return of Christ
topics.question: Is Jesus really coming back?
topics.summary: Yes. No one knows the day or hour, so live ready: watching, working and waiting.
topics.guidance: Daniel saw one like the Son of man coming with the clouds of heaven. Jesus promised to come again and warned that no one knows when, so we should be ready. The apostles waited eagerly for him, explained that his delay is God's patience, giving time to repent, and ended the Bible with a prayer: come, Lord Jesus.

teachings.note: I will come again and receive you to myself.
teachings.text: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

teachings.note: No one knows the day or the hour.
teachings.text: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

teachings.note: Watch and be ready, because he comes at an hour you don't expect.
teachings.text: Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.  But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up.  Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.

teachings.note: One like the Son of man comes with the clouds, and his kingdom never ends.
teachings.text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

teachings.note: The Lord will descend from heaven, and we will be with him for ever.
teachings.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.

teachings.note: God isn't slow; he is patient, wanting everyone to repent.
teachings.text: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

teachings.note: Surely I come quickly. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus.
teachings.text: He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

topics.practice: If Jesus came back tomorrow, what would you want to have put right today?
topics.prayer: Even so, come, Lord Jesus. Keep me ready and faithful until you do.

topics.name: Judgement
topics.question: Will I have to answer for my life?
topics.summary: Everyone will give account to God. But whoever trusts Christ has passed from death to life and does not come into condemnation.
topics.guidance: The Preacher ends by reminding us that God will bring every work into judgement. Jesus spoke of the Son of man separating the nations, and the apostles say we will each give account of ourselves. But Jesus also promised that whoever hears his word and believes will not come into condemnation. Judgement is real, and so is mercy.

teachings.note: Fear God and keep his commandments; every deed will be judged.
teachings.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man. For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

teachings.note: The Son of man will come in glory and separate the nations.
teachings.text: When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:  And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:

teachings.note: Whoever hears and believes has passed from death to life, and will not be condemned.
teachings.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.

teachings.note: We must all appear before the judgement seat of Christ.
teachings.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

teachings.note: Each of us will give account of himself to God.
teachings.text: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

teachings.note: We die once and then face judgement; Christ was offered once to bear our sins.
teachings.text: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.

topics.practice: Live today as someone who will give account, and who is already forgiven.
topics.prayer: Lord, I will stand before you one day. Thank you that in Christ I have passed from death to life.

topics.name: All things new
topics.question: How does the story end?
topics.summary: With a new heaven and a new earth, where God lives with his people, and there is no more death, crying or pain.
topics.guidance: The prophets saw a coming world with no more war, where the wolf lies down with the lamb and the earth is full of the knowledge of God. Jesus taught us to pray for that kingdom to come on earth as in heaven. The Bible ends where it began, in a garden city, with God wiping every tear away and saying, 'Behold, I make all things new.'

teachings.note: God will create new heavens and a new earth.
teachings.text: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.

teachings.note: Swords will be beaten into ploughshares; nations will learn war no more.
teachings.text: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

teachings.note: The earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD.
teachings.text: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.

teachings.note: Pray: your kingdom come, your will be done on earth as in heaven.
teachings.text: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

teachings.note: We look for new heavens and a new earth, where righteousness lives.
teachings.text: Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.

teachings.note: God will live with his people, wipe away every tear, and make all things new.
teachings.text: And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful.

topics.practice: Do one thing this week that looks like the world to come: make peace, heal, or give.
topics.prayer: Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
